english.title: Use military uniform to gain entry to prohibited place or for interest prejudicial to state
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), for

(A)_[the purpose of gaining admission to **(..SPECIFY PLACE..), a prohibited place]_
(B)_[the purpose of assisting another person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), to gain admission to **(..SPECIFY PLACE..), a prohibited place]_
(C)_[a purpose prejudicial to the safety or interests of the state]_

within the meaning of the Official Secrets Act 1911,

(D)_[used or wore, without lawful authority,]_
(E)_[falsely represented yourself to be a person who was entitled to use or wear]_
(F)_[falsely represented yourself to be a person who had been entitled to use or wear]_

a military uniform or a uniform so nearly resembling the same as to be calculated to deceive
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1)(a) and 8(2) of the Official Secrets Act 1920.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Whilst this offence is triable either way, it should usually be dealt with on indictment. The offence may only be dealt with summarily with the consent of the Attorney General (section 8(2) Official Secrets Act 1920).

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
